hints: Particle $A$ moves on a smooth horizontal surface pulled by tension $T$: $T = m_A a = 0.3a$.
Particle $B$ moves down the smooth slope with downslope gravitational force $m_B g\sin\theta = 1.5(10)(3/5) = 9\text{ N}$.
Write Newton's second law for $B$: $9 - T = 1.5a$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$: $9 = 1.8a \implies a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, then find $T = 0.3(5) = 1.5\text{ N}$.
walkthrough: State Newton's second law of motion for connected particles: apply $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ to each body along its line of motion.

For particle $A$ on the smooth horizontal surface, tension $T$ is the only horizontal force:
$$T = m_A a \implies T = 0.3a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

For particle $B$ on the smooth inclined plane, the forward force down the slope is the downslope weight component:
$$W_{B,\text{slope}} = m_B g\sin\theta = 1.5 \times 10 \times \frac{3}{5} = 9\text{ N}$$

Write the equation of motion for $B$ moving down the slope:
$$9 - T = m_B a \implies 9 - T = 1.5a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate the tension $T$:
$$T + (9 - T) = 0.3a + 1.5a$$
$$9 = (0.3 + 1.5)a = 1.8a$$

Divide both sides by $1.8$ to find the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{9}{1.8} = \frac{90}{18} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ back into Equation 1 to find tension $T$:
$$T = 0.3 \times 5 = 1.5\text{ N}$$

hints: Use the kinematics data for the accelerated motion: starting from rest ($u = 0$), reaching $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $t = 3\text{ s}$ gives $a = \frac{v - u}{t} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Find the normal reaction forces: for horizontal particle $A$, $R_A = m_A g = 0.3 \times 10 = 3\text{ N}$. For inclined particle $B$, $\cos\theta = \sqrt{1 - (3/5)^2} = \frac{4}{5}$, so $R_B = m_B g\cos\theta = 1.5 \times 10 \times \frac{4}{5} = 12\text{ N}$.
Express the friction forces in terms of $\mu$: $F_A = \mu R_A = 3\mu$ and $F_B = \mu R_B = 12\mu$, both opposing the motion.
Apply Newton's second law to the entire system along the string: $m_B g\sin\theta - F_A - F_B = (m_A + m_B)a \implies 9 - 3\mu - 12\mu = 1.8(5/3)$, and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
State the SUVAT velocity-time equation to determine the common acceleration of the particles:
$$v = u + at$$

Substitute initial velocity $u = 0$, final velocity $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and time $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$5 = 0 + 3a \implies a = \frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.67\text{ m s}^{-2} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

Determine the normal reaction on horizontal particle $A$:
$$R_A = m_A g = 0.3 \times 10 = 3\text{ N}$$

Determine the normal reaction on inclined particle $B$. Since $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$, use $\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}$:
$$R_B = m_B g\cos\theta = 1.5 \times 10 \times \frac{4}{5} = 12\text{ N}$$

Write expressions for the friction force on each particle using $F = \mu R$:
$$F_A = 3\mu$$
$$F_B = 12\mu$$

Set up the equation of motion for particle $A$ moving horizontally rightwards:
$$T - F_A = m_A a \implies T - 3\mu = 0.3\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = 0.5 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the equation of motion for particle $B$ moving down the inclined plane:
$$m_B g\sin\theta - T - F_B = m_B a$$
$$9 - T - 12\mu = 1.5\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = 2.5 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate string tension $T$:
$$(T - 3\mu) + (9 - T - 12\mu) = 0.5 + 2.5$$
$$9 - 15\mu = 3$$

Divide both sides by $15$ to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{6}{15} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$
